terms.grammar: phrase: committō, committere, commīsī, commissum with proelium (or pugnam, certāmen)
evidence: Caes. BG 2.21: proeliī committendī signum dare (Lewis & Short)
Nep. Eum. 3: in aciem exercitum ēdūxit proeliumque commīsit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Committere on its own is “bring together, join”, and also “entrust” and “commit (a crime)” (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: come to close quarters, come to blows
terms.grammar: phrase: cōnserō, cōnserere, cōnseruī, cōnsertum with manum, cum and the ablative or inter sē
evidence: Cic. Mur. 20: signa contulit, manum cōnseruit, magnās cōpiās hostium fūdit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Hand-to-hand fighting; cōnserere alone is “join, fasten together”, and with proelium or pugnam it is the same as committere (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: signa contulit, manum cōnseruit, magnās cōpiās hostium fūdit
phrases.english: he joined battle, came to close quarters and routed great forces of the enemy

phrases.latin: in aciem exercitum ēdūxit proeliumque commīsit
phrases.english: he led his army out into line and engaged
